# Chapter 3 Data Summary

This chapter summarizes the financial viability of the field work that was conducted at the SCRA. The main questions are as follows:

**1. What are the financial benefits of increasingly systems-oriented management?**

- H0: There are no differences in financial benefits across the I-S continuum.

- H1: Increasingly systems-oriented practices have lower financial benefits due to lower yields

- H2: Increasingly systems-oriented practices have equal financial benefits to more input-oriented practices due to premium organic prices.

- **Sub topic:** include sensory analysis & willingness-to-pay in analysis. This is Alexa's work - don't analyze, just cite.

**2. What are the financial costs of increasingly systems-oriented management?**

- H1: there are no differences in financial costs across the I-S continuum.

- H2: Systems-oriented treatments will cost more than input-oriented treatments due to higher labour costs.

**3. What is the return-on-investment for increasingly systems-oriented management?**

- H0: there are no differences in ROI across the I-S continuum.

- H1: Input-oriented treatments will have higher ROI due to lower labour costs and higher yields.

## Background Information

### Statistics Canada (2021)

The latest Stats Canada report from 2021 stated the following:

- 189,874 farms across Canada (decreased 1.9% from 2016). 3.2% decrease in total farm area from 2016.

- Oilseed and grain farms are the largest proportion - 65,135 oilseed and grain farms, accounting for 34.3% of total farms. Followed by beef and feedlots (20.9%) - 82.7% of farms are either beef or oilseed/grain (127.1 million acres).

- Farm: unit that produces agricultural products and reports revenues and expenses for tax purposes to the CRA.

- Farm consolidation continues - 9.9% of farms have sales of \>\$1 million. Farms reporting at least \$2 million in sales account for 51.5% of total farm operating revenues.

- Mean age of farmers in 2021: 56 years. Median: 58 years.

- Land access is an issue. Total market value of land and buildings for farms in Canada is \$603.8 billion in 2021.

- 64.5% of farms report some use of practices such as winter grazing, rotational grazing, plowing down green crops, winter cover crops, and shelterbreaks.

- 1.1 million head of sheep in 2021. 9.6% less farms; 8,487 farms report sheep and lambs.

- Greenhouse area: 330.5 million square feet n 2021. 219.7 million square feet for fruits and vegetables.

- **FARMS INCUR 83 CENTS OF EXPENSES FOR EVERY DOLLAR OF REVENUE.** Farm operating revenues totalled \$87 billion in 2020, while expenses reached \$72.2 billion. Oilseed and grain farms were the most profitable with expenses-to-revenues ratio of 0.76, while sheep and goat farms had the highest ratio (0.97).

- **SMALLER FARMS ARE MORE RELIANT ON DIRECT SALES**. Farms with less than \$10,000 in sales accounted for nearly half of farms in which direct sales represented more than three quarters of total farm operating revenues. Farms with \>\$2 million accounted for 0.8% of farms in which direct sales represented more than 3/4 of total revenues.

- 47.7% of farm operators reported off-farm work (125,280) in 2020.

### Towards Increased Profits (TIP) Report Benchmark

The [TIP program](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/industry/agriculture-seafood/business-market-development/agrifood-business-management/running-a-farm-business/towards-increased-profits-report) provides several sheets for different sectors. The vegetable sector file for 2022 provided the following information:

| Revenue Class | Year | n | Total Arm's Length Salary | Total Allowable Expenses | Total Non-Allowable Expenses | Total Expenses | Net Margin |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| \$0-50K | 2017-2021 | 21 | 19.5% | 37.91% | 71.78% | 103.16% | **-3.16%** |
| \$0-50K | 2022 | 21 | 12.69% | 40.44% | 96.35% | 137.16% | **-37.16%** |
| \$50-500K | 2017-2021 | 43 | 28.17% | 40.94% | 38.26% | 90.50% | **5.53%** |
| \$50-500K | 2022 | 43 | 30.09% | 45.16% | 43.01% | 91.27% | **8.73%** |
| \$500K-1M | 2017-2021 | 15 | 35.18% | 55.91% | 28.42% | 85.43% | **14.57%** |
| \$500K-1M | 2022 | 15 | 35.53% | 56.82% | 32.53% | 92.75% | **7.25%** |
| \$1M+ | 2017-2021 | 41 | 22.07% | 53.49% | 30.39% | 90.04% | **7.49%** |
| \$1M+ | 2022 | 41 | 23.80% | 56.49% | 33.38% | 95.53% | **4.47%** |

The TIP report is based on data from the CRA. The farm type is classified when more than half of total farm sales come from sales of a specific commodity or group of like commodities (e.g. 52% grain and 48% cow/calf results in a farm classified as grain).

Industry benchmarks are derived fro the AgriStability and AgriInvest participant data supplied to BC from the CRA. Each industry benchmark is the median from the group of ranked farms of that type and size.

The report uses income and expense information provided to the CRA (mostly from the cash method of accounting). Cash accounting does not reflect fiscal year adjustments for changes in inventory, accounts receivable, or accounts payable and may show income tax management rather than farm management performance.

Gross farming income is the sum of allowable and non-allowable income (as defined by the AgriStability program). Allowable income consists of commodity sales and program payments. Non-allowable income consists of other farm income, e.g. 9601 Agricultural contact work. GFI does not reflect accrual adjustments for changes in inventory or accounts receivable for cash tax filers.

Expenses for the TIP report are classified as allowable and non-allowable expenses.

Net margin for the TIP report is computed as GFI - total expenses (GFI includes both allowable and non-allowable income and total expenses).

## Question 1: Financial Benefits

This section summarizes the analytic direction that is used to analyze the financial benefits of the work. The approach for all following sections is as follows:

1.  Create Excel sheet summarizing all the ROI details for 2022-2024
2.  Upload to R.
3.  Summarize for each year and treatment (graphically and numerically).
4.  Test treatment \~ indicator effects with a LMM (e.g. lmer(yield \~ treatment + (1\|year), REML = FALSE, na.action = na.omit).
5.  Test posthoc with emmeans and Sidak adjustment for any statistically relevant models.
6.  Create graphic that summarizes everything, e.g. a heatmap or a forest plot that shows T1 (0) vs T2-5.

The code below is a function that produces summaries and bar graphs for all indicators based on year and treatment.

## Function Code

```{r Plot&Summary-Function}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(rlang)   # for enquo / as_name
library(scales)  # for dollar_format if you want $ axis

# Optional helper
`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (!is.null(x)) x else y

TREAT_LABELS <- c(
  "Treatment 1",
  "Treatment 2",
  "Treatment 3",
  "Treatment 4",
  "Treatment 5"
)

# 1) Generic summary: mean ± SE by year × treatment (+ "All" row)
summarise_treat_year <- function(data, var) {
  var_quo <- enquo(var)

  per_year <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!var_quo)) %>%
    group_by(year, treatment) %>%
    summarise(
      n    = sum(!is.na(!!var_quo)),
      mean = mean(!!var_quo, na.rm = TRUE),
      se   = sd(!!var_quo,   na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(year = as.character(year))

  all_years <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!var_quo)) %>%
    group_by(treatment) %>%
    summarise(
      n    = sum(!is.na(!!var_quo)),
      mean = mean(!!var_quo, na.rm = TRUE),
      se   = sd(!!var_quo,   na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(year = "All")

  bind_rows(per_year, all_years) %>%
    mutate(
      treatment = factor(treatment, levels = 1:5, labels = TREAT_LABELS),
      year      = factor(year, levels = c(sort(unique(per_year$year)), "All"))
    ) %>%
    arrange(year, treatment)
}

# 2) Generic gt summary table
make_treat_year_table <- function(data, var, outcome_label = NULL,
                                  digits_mean = 1, digits_se = 1) {

  var_quo <- enquo(var)
  label   <- outcome_label %||% as_name(var_quo)

  smry <- summarise_treat_year(data, !!var_quo) %>%
    mutate(
      summary = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits_mean, "f ± %.", digits_se, "f"),
                        mean, se)
    )

  table_data <- smry %>%
    select(year, treatment, summary) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = summary)

  gt(table_data, rowname_col = "year") %>%
    tab_header(
      title    = md(paste0("**", label, "**")),
      subtitle = "Mean ± SE by year × treatment"
    ) %>%
    fmt_missing(everything(), missing_text = "—") %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_stub(rows = "All")
    ) %>%
    tab_options(
      table.font.size   = px(14),
      data_row.padding  = px(3)
    )
}

# 3) Generic bar plot
plot_treat_year_bar <- function(data, var,
                                outcome_label = NULL,
                                dollar_scale  = FALSE) {

  var_quo <- enquo(var)
  label   <- outcome_label %||% as_name(var_quo)

  smry <- summarise_treat_year(data, !!var_quo)
  pd   <- position_dodge(width = 0.75)

  p <- ggplot(smry, aes(x = treatment, y = mean, fill = year)) +
    geom_col(position = pd, width = 0.7) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
                  position = pd, width = 0.2) +
      scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Greens") +
    labs(
      x     = "Treatment",
      y     = paste0(label, " (mean ± SE)"),
      fill  = "Year",
      title = paste0(label, " — by treatment and year")
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

  if (dollar_scale) {
    p <- p + scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format())
  }

  p
}

```

```{r}
check_diagnostics <- function(model, data = NULL) {
  
  if (inherits(model, "formula")) {
    if (is.null(data)) stop("If providing a formula, you must supply data.")
    model <- lm(model, data = data, na.action = na.exclude)
  }
  
  if (!inherits(model, "lm"))
    stop("Model must be an lm object or a formula.")
  
  mf <- model.frame(model)
  df <- data.frame(
    resid  = residuals(model),
    fitted = fitted(model),
    mf
  )
  df <- df[!is.na(df$resid), ]
  
  if (!is.null(data)) {
    treatment_names <- c("treatment", "Treatment", "trt", "Trt")
    trt_col <- treatment_names[treatment_names %in% names(data)][1]
    
    if (!is.na(trt_col)) {
      df$treatment <- factor(data[[trt_col]][match(rownames(df), rownames(data))])
    }
    
    if ("year" %in% names(data)) {
      df$year <- factor(data$year[match(rownames(df), rownames(data))])
    }
    
    if ("treatment" %in% names(df) && "year" %in% names(df)) {
      df$trt_year <- interaction(df$treatment, df$year, sep = "_")
    }
  }
  
  group_vars <- c("treatment", "year", "trt_year")
  group_vars <- group_vars[group_vars %in% names(df)]
  
  shapiro_result <- shapiro.test(df$resid)
  cat("Shapiro-Wilk test for residuals:\n")
  cat("W =", round(shapiro_result$statistic, 4),
      "| p-value =", round(shapiro_result$p.value, 4), "\n\n")
  
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
  
  car::qqPlot(df$resid, main = "Q-Q Plot",
              ylab = "Residuals", col = "black", pch = 19)
  
  hist(df$resid, breaks = 30, freq = FALSE,
       main = "Residuals", xlab = "Residuals", col = "grey")
  lines(density(df$resid), col = "red", lwd = 2)
  
  plot(df$fitted, df$resid,
       xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Residuals",
       main = "Residuals vs Fitted", pch = 19)
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
  
  slots_remaining <- 3
  i <- 1
  while (i <= slots_remaining) {
    if (i <= length(group_vars)) {
      gv <- group_vars[i]
      boxplot(df$resid ~ df[[gv]],
              main = paste("Residuals by", gv),
              xlab = gv, ylab = "Residuals")
      abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
    } else {
      plot.new()
    }
    i <- i + 1
  }
  
  invisible(list(
    model      = model,
    shapiro    = shapiro_result,
    residual_df = df
  ))
}

# ---- 4. PLOT MODEL PREDICTIONS WITH RAW VALUES ------------------
plot_pred_with_raw <- function(model, data, response_var,
                               x           = "treatment",
                               facet_by    = "year",
                               y_label     = NULL,
                               point_alpha = 0.4,
                               point_size  = 2) {
  
  if (is.null(y_label)) y_label <- response_var
  
  newdat <- expand_grid(
    treatment = unique(data$treatment),
    year      = unique(data$year)
  )
  
  p <- predict(model, newdata = newdat, se.fit = TRUE, re.form = NA)
  
  preds <- newdat %>%
    mutate(
      fit   = p$fit,
      se    = p$se.fit,
      lower = fit - 1.96 * se,
      upper = fit + 1.96 * se
    )
  
  raw <- data %>%
    select(treatment, year, all_of(response_var)) %>%
    rename(y = all_of(response_var))
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_jitter(
      data  = raw,
      aes(x = .data[[x]], y = y),
      width = 0.1,
      alpha = point_alpha,
      size  = point_size,
      color = "grey40"
    ) +
    geom_errorbar(
      data = preds,
      aes(x = .data[[x]], ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
      width     = 0.15,
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = preds,
      aes(x = .data[[x]], y = fit),
      size = 3
    ) +
    facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", facet_by))) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1, style_negative = "minus")
    ) +
    labs(
      x     = "Treatment",
      y     = y_label,
      title = paste("Fitted Model Predictions + Raw Data for", response_var)
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14)
}
```

### Yield - Bean

```{r Yield-Bean}
plot_treat_year_bar(
  dat,
  bean,
  outcome_label = "Bean Yield (g)",
  dollar_scale  = FALSE
)

make_treat_year_table(
  dat,
  bean,
  outcome_label = "Bean Yield (g)"
)
```

```{r Yield-Bean-LM}
beanmod <- lm(bean ~ treatment + year, data = dat)
summary(beanmod)
```

```{r Yield-Bean-ANOVA}
car::Anova(beanmod, type=2)
```

No significant bean \~ treatment effects. Year is significant. Posthoc is as follows.

```{r Yield-Bean-Year-EMMpairs}
emm_bean <- emmeans(beanmod, ~ year)
bean_pairs <- pairs(emm_bean, adjust = "sidak")
print(bean_pairs)

```

```{r Yield-Bean-Year-CLD}
cld <- emmeans:::cld.emmGrid
cld_bean <- cld(emm_bean, adjust = "sidak", Letters = letters)
cld_bean <- cld_bean %>%
  arrange(year) %>%
  mutate(
    rank = row_number(),
    year = factor(year, levels = c(2022,2023,2024)),
    emmean = round(emmean, 4),
    SE = round(SE, 4),
    df = round(df, 4),
    lower.CL = round(lower.CL, 4), 
    upper.CL = round(upper.CL, 4)
  )
print(cld_bean)
```

2023 had the highest bean yields (3035g higher than 2022, 1418g higher than 2024).

## Question 3: ROI

### Total ROI - Wholesale

```{r ROI-Wholesale, echo=FALSE}
plot_treat_year_bar(
  dat,
  ROIwholesale,
  outcome_label = "Wholesale ROI",
  dollar_scale  = TRUE
)

make_treat_year_table(
  dat,
  ROIwholesale,
  outcome_label = "Wholesale ROI"
)

```

```{r ROI-Wholesale-LM, echo=FALSE}
margins_wholemod <- lm(margins_whole ~ treatment * year, data = dat)
summary(margins_wholemod)
```

```{r ROI-Wholesale-ANOVA, echo=FALSE}
car::Anova(ROIwholemod, type=2)
```

```{r WholesaleROI-Normality, echo=FALSE}
check_diagnostics(ROIwholemod, dat)
```

```{r WholesaleROI-Model-With-Raw, echo=FALSE}
plot_pred_with_raw(
  ROIwholemod, 
  dat, 
  response_var = "ROIwholesale",
  y_label = "Wholesale ROI (%)"
)
```

Significant treatment effect. Conduct post-hoc.

```{r Wholesale-Emmeans, echo=FALSE}
emm_wholesaleROI <- emmeans(margins_wholemod, ~ treatment * year)

#Treatment differences within each year
pairs(emm_wholesaleROI, by = "year", adjust = "tukey")
```

```{r ROI-Wholesale-CLD, echo=FALSE}
emm_treat_by_year <- emmeans(totalYieldmod, ~ treatment | year)

cld_totalyield <- emmeans:::cld.emmGrid(
  emm_treat_by_year,
  adjust  = "tukey",
  Letters = letters
)

cld_totalyield
```

```{r}
library(lmerTest)

# Make sure dat has no NAs in ROIdirect, treatment, year
dat_complete <- subset(dat, !is.na(ROIdirect) & !is.na(treatment) & !is.na(year))

m1 <- lm(totalYield ~ treatment, data = dat_complete)

m2 <- lm(totalYield ~ treatment + year, data = dat_complete)

m3 <- lm(totalYield ~ treatment * year, data = dat_complete)

m4 <- lmer(totalYield ~ treatment + (1 | year),
           data = dat_complete,
           REML = FALSE)
AIC(m1, m2, m3, m4)
```
